Scan saver while screen off / locked

While the screen is off or on the lock screen, battery-refresh scans are skipped entirely. This takes priority over the refresh interval below. The moment you unlock, if more time has passed than the refresh interval, the battery refreshes right away.

While the app is open the battery is scanned continuously. When it is closed, it scans briefly on this interval instead. Between scans the last known value is shown. Turning the screen on or unlocking also triggers a quick refresh; if "scan saver" above is on, the interval is ignored while the screen is off or locked.\n\n⚠ Intervals under 1 minute keep Bluetooth scanning almost constantly and noticeably increase phone battery drain.
Fast scan on periodic refresh too

Periodic refresh scans also run at full speed for their first 15 seconds. Turn off to avoid that extra power use. Right after AirPods connect the app always scans at full speed regardless of this setting.

Keeps a separate control link (L2CAP) to the AirPods so noise control, ear detection, conversation awareness and other settings can be read and changed. If you only need the battery display, turn this off to save the power and connection overhead of that always-on link. The items on the "AirPods settings" screen will then be hidden.
Read battery over the control channel

The default battery display reads the Bluetooth advertisement (beacon) the AirPods broadcast nearby. That beacon carries no device identifier and its MAC address keeps rotating, so if someone next to you is also using AirPods there is no way to be completely sure which reading is yours, and when the screen is off and scan saver kicks in the value arrives late.

With this on, whenever the "Hardware control channel" above is connected the battery is requested directly over that channel. The channel is established only with the exact AirPods paired to this phone, so readings can never be mixed up, and left/right/case levels come through even while Bluetooth scanning is off.

On devices where the control channel does not connect (unsupported model, failed link) it automatically falls back to the beacon method. Requires the "Hardware control channel" above to be on.

When AirPods connect (or when you run the shortcut), a pill with the AirPods and their battery slides in at the top of the screen for a few seconds. Needs the "display over other apps" permission.

Once the alert / island has been shown, the app shuts itself down completely instead of staying in the background. Battery is then read again only on reconnect, from a shortcut (Galaxy Routines) or when you open the app or tap the widget. The persistent notification and periodic refresh are disabled while this is on.
Without the "Nearby devices" permission the app cannot read the AirPods battery at all. Please allow it.
Turn this off if you trigger the island from Galaxy Routines or a shortcut instead. The app then ignores Bluetooth connection broadcasts entirely, so nothing wakes it up in the background.
Not used in on-demand mode (no periodic refresh, no resident service)
The island and the alert are both off, so nothing will be shown when AirPods connect
